name: Lemon Balm
grown_as: A hardy perennial herb grown for its lemon-scented leaves. Plain green form; a golden-leaved variety exists. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A bushy clump 30 to 80 cm high and as wide, of many upright, branched, square, slightly hairy stems from a woody crown. Seeds itself freely.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, each pair at right angles to the one below
leaf.outline: Broadly oval, 3 to 7 cm long, almost as wide near the base, the lower leaves the broadest
leaf.base: Rounded to cut straight across, sometimes faintly heart-shaped
leaf.margin: Coarse, even, rounded teeth all round from just above the base to the tip
leaf.veins: Side veins and a fine net of smaller veins all pressed in, so the leaf is deeply quilted
leaf.surface: Wrinkled, matt, thinly hairy; paler beneath
leaf.stalk: 1 to 4 cm, longest on the lower leaves
leaf.colour: Fresh light green, a little yellowish

flower.petals: Joined; a short notched upper lip and a three-lobed lower lip
flower.colour: White, pale yellow in bud, sometimes tinged pale pink or lilac
flower.centre: Four stamens hidden under the upper lip
flower.behind: A hairy, two-lipped, bell-shaped green calyx, larger than the flower looks
flower.carried: In small loose clusters in the joints of the upper leaves, half hidden among them, often all on one side of the stem; not in a spike

fruit: Four small dark brown nutlets in each dry calyx, left in clusters up the old stems. Seeds: tiny shiny dark brown seeds about 1.5 mm long, oval with one end narrower.
seedling: Two small round to oval seed leaves on short stalks; then rounded true leaves with round teeth, opposite.
winter: Dies down to the ground; in mild winters a low tuft of small leaves stays at the crown.

leaf: a broad oval leaf on a clear stalk
even rounded teeth all round the edge
deeply quilted surface with a net of pressed-in veins
bloom: small white two-lipped flowers in a cluster at a leaf joint
a hairy green calyx behind each
seed: tiny shiny dark brown oval seeds
seedling: first true leaves rounded with round teeth
young: a low clump of broad round-toothed leaves in opposite pairs on stalks
crop: a bushy clump of upright branched stems thick with broad quilted leaves
flower: small white flowers in clusters at the upper leaf joints, among the leaves
seedhead: clusters of brown dry calyces in the leaf joints of the old stems
dormant: cut down or dead stems with a low tuft of small leaves at the crown, or bare soil

look_alikes: Mint has narrower, sharply toothed leaves and flowers in end spikes. Catnip is grey and downy with flowers in end spikes. White dead-nettle has larger white flowers in rings and hairier, more pointed leaves. Stinging nettle has longer, sharply toothed, stinging leaves. Crushed lemon balm smells of lemon.
